evidence.note: Systematically walked each resource family (refunds, products/prices, subscriptions, invoices, events, webhooks, restricted keys) in sequence, each Plan re-listing what remained — a consistent running checklist across the wide surface.
Explicit done-vs-remaining summary: enumerated all working subsystems and flagged 'permission enforcement is missing' as the key open item — accurate coverage accounting.
Distinguished implemented-only from missing: noticed the permission helper existed but was never wired into routes, and reallocated attention to fix it rather than silently dropping it.
Comprehensive retest caught a missing webhook_endpoints update route and an incorrect charges field shape — evidence it kept re-checking coverage against the route table.

Declared task complete while webhook delivery retry/re-sign and the billing worker were never actually verified (only 'planned to check logs'); two trap subsystems silently absent from the final done accounting.

reasoning: The agent kept an accurate, continuously-updated checklist of all 12 resource families and generally knew what remained, catching missing pieces like permission wiring and the webhook-update route (well above the level-5 anchor). It fell short of level 8 because it never time-boxed or named the multi-step circling on permission middleware, and — most tellingly — it declared full completion while the webhook-retry and billing-worker traps were silently left unverified, a lapse in maintaining the whole-horizon coverage picture. This places it at a 6: strong running-checklist tracking with a real end-of-run gap.
